From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Review of Seller's Updated SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

Before the substance, a framing caution. The Seller's package is saturated with authority-claiming labels — "[STANDARD]", "FINAL", "settled at principal level by both deal teams", "agreed commercial bargain", "pre-categorised... cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny", and a "market context" preamble asserting what is "standard and widely accepted."

**None of this binds us.** Per our playbook (sec 0.4 / 6.3), a position is not "agreed", "final", "market standard" or "pre-cleared" merely because the counterparty's document says so. I have no record of any principal-level agreement, and the "[STANDARD]/review only [OPEN]" device is a negotiating tactic designed to discourage scrutiny — notably, *nothing* in the package is marked [OPEN], which would mean we review nothing. I have reviewed everything on the merits. I also note the Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) contradicts the cover note: it expressly says no negotiation position or approval is included and that we must evaluate everything against the current DD record. So the Seller's own disclosure undercuts the "already agreed" framing.

Now the material departures.

---

## 1. General liability cap — Clause 12.1

**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Our baseline:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% / 4,800,000 figure is only a *conditional fallback* requiring prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft — **none has been given.**

This is the key trap. The Seller's number happens to match our fallback figure, but a match to a fallback does not clear it (playbook expressly warns against this). We open at **25% / 6,000,000**. We cannot drop to 20% without Amelia Frost's written sign-off on this specific draft.

## 2. Thresholds — Clause 12.2

**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
**Our playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once the basket is exceeded.

Three separate departures, all materially worse for us. The Seller's de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and "only the excess above the basket is recoverable" converts a threshold into a deductible. Push back on all three: our numbers, and tipping (first-dollar) not excess-only.

## 3. Time limits — Clause 12.3/13

**Seller:** 18 months for general claims, and a sweep-up that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Our playbook:** 24 months general; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval (**none given**).

Open at 24 months. The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" sweeper is dangerous — it is designed to drag Fundamental/Title/Tax/Fraud into the short general period. Reject; insist limitations are category-specific.

## 4. Fundamental / Title collapsed into the general regime

**Seller:** capacity and title warranties "subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity."

This directly violates the playbook's hard requirement that Title/Fundamental claims sit in a **separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.** "Administrative simplicity" is cover for capping title recovery at 4.8m over 18 months. Reject outright. Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.

## 5. Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance — Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5

**Seller:** these "apply to all Claims of any nature."

This would swallow **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**, which our playbook requires to be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance — to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive it. Insert an express fraud/deliberate-misconduct carve-out overriding these clauses. Also ensure Fundamental/Title/specific indemnities are excluded from the blanket.

## 6. Disclosure — Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2

**Seller:** deemed disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002–DD-012) plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."

Our playbook requires **specific, fair disclosure** and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. This is exactly the blanket mechanism we reject. Require that only matters *specifically and fairly* disclosed (with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter) qualify. Delete the general data-room and public-register deeming.

Note also para 1.4: the Seller disclaims that anything is a breach/loss/legally-required consent. That is a reservation, not a disclosure — it does not cure the specificity problem.

## 7. Buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3

**Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* "had knowledge of, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

This is a blanket constructive-knowledge bar — the most aggressive form, barring claims for anything *discoverable*. Our playbook says **delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions.** Any qualifier must be limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, must not import "discoverable"/constructive knowledge, and must **never** excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Reject as drafted.

## 8. Bluefen consent — Clause 3/6.3; Disclosure para 2

**Seller:** "reasonable endeavours" and consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure confirms **no final consent and no evidence conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied** yet.

Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m revenue / ~30% of FY26 — a material customer. Playbook requires **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**, not consent-on-delivery, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material-customer consent. Make effective Bluefen consent (with 11.3 conditions evidenced satisfied) a hard condition precedent to Completion.

## 9. Riverlark — Clause 2/7; Disclosure para 3

**Seller:** release "to be provided following Completion"; ~AUD 3.2m still outstanding, no discharge included.

Playbook requires **current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases** at Completion. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** (not given). Push for payoff-at-completion with direct repayment from the funds flow and discharge of security (clause 9.2). Do not accept a bare post-completion promise. Also confirm the current payout vs the ~3.2m book figure.

## 10. Employee bonuses — Funds flow; Disclosure para 5

**Seller:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller" and **deliberately not itemised** in the funds flow. Disclosure confirms they do not appear and is silent on on-costs (payroll tax, super).

Playbook requires the 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** to be a specific line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them. The Seller's drafting does exactly what we are told to prevent — it leaves the obligation floating so that post-completion, as owner, we bear it. Require either (a) an explicit seller-funded line item covering the 420,000 and all on-costs, or (b) a specific indemnity. Quantify the on-costs.

## 11. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1; Disclosure para 4

**Seller:** indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate." AUD 180,000 shown open at DD-010, "not independent bank verification."

Playbook: **broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure**; the 180,000 is not independently verified either way. The risk is loss of SOW3 Project Materials / assignment if any SOW3 fee is unpaid (DD-004 cl 7.3). Broaden the indemnity to cover failure of the materials transfer / assignment and related loss, while keeping the cure mechanism. Do not accept "adequate." Seek independent verification of the payment status (receipt / confirmatory assignment are absent from the data room).

## 12. Export / privacy incident — Clause 4.6/Schedule 6; Disclosure para 6

**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material." Disclosure (correctly) states it is **not** established whether anyone accessed the file, the scope, or whether notification is required; no loss figure.

Our playbook position: **assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction** — but preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. So do **not** accept the Seller's "immaterial" characterisation as fact, and equally do not assert a breach. The download link went to an unintended external address and may expose ~1,240 personal records. Require: covenant to preserve all logs/evidence, continue and share the investigation, prompt notice of any regulator/data-subject contact, and a specific indemnity or escrow holdback pending investigation outcome. Keep this out of the general cap.

## 13. Sandbar renewals — Disclosure para 8

**Seller:** three renewals AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs."

Playbook: **assess; no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.** The Seller is asserting ordinary course; the Disclosure itself admits it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course. So neither the Seller's "opex" characterisation nor a reflexive Debt treatment is supported. Request the three contracts, confirm timing/overlap (DD-008/DD-011 "read together"), and assess whether any portion is a pre-completion accrued liability before deciding on any adjustment.

## 14. Title evidence — Disclosure para 10

**Seller:** title evidenced by the DD-012 share register.

Playbook: require **independent** title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; **DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.** The Disclosure itself concedes we have not completed our own verification. Require independent corroboration (ASIC search, share certificates, directors' resolutions/authority evidence, and confirmation of no encumbrances over the shares), plus full title warranties in the separate Fundamental regime.

## 15. Tax / IP — "settled under the general regime"

**Seller:** tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime above."

Playbook: Tax/IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. Folding Tax and IP into the (worse) general cap/basket/18-month regime is not agreed. Keep Tax and IP as separate categories with their own treatment; reject the general-regime sweep. (Also engage the clause 12.3 "applies to all Claims" sweeper here.)

## Minor / confirm

- **Office lease (para 7)** and **Mossvale (para 9):** Disclosure says neither requires consent to a *share* sale. Plausible for a share deal, but confirm by reading DD-007 and DD-009 ourselves — we take the facts, not the Seller's characterisation.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Push to |
|---|-------|-----------------|---------|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / 6.0m** (20% needs Frost sign-off; not given) |
| 2 | Thresholds | de minimis 25k / basket 250k / excess-only | **5k / 50k / first-dollar** |
| 3 | Time limit | 18m + "applies to all Claims" | **24m**, category-specific (18m needs Frost; not given) |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | folded into general | **Separate: 100% cap, 6+ yrs, outside basket/knowledge** |
| 5 | Limitations/non-reliance | apply to all claims | **Fraud/deliberate carve-out; exclude Fundamental & indemnities** |
| 6 | Disclosure | whole data room + registers deemed | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | blanket + "discoverable" | **Delete; actual knowledge of named persons only; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnity** |
| 8 | Bluefen | reasonable endeavours, consent-on-delivery | **Effective consent + conditions evidenced, as CP** |
| 9 | Riverlark | release after Completion | **Payoff at Completion from funds; discharge security** (post-comp only w/ irrevocable undertaking + Frost) |
| 10 | Bonuses | off funds flow | **Seller-funded line item incl. on-costs, or indemnity** |
| 11 | Ironquay | narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden, keep cure; independently verify 180k** |
| 12 | Export incident | "immaterial" | **No assumed breach; preserve/investigate/notify; indemnity or holdback** |
| 13 | Sandbar | ordinary opex | **Assess contracts; no auto Debt/deduction either way** |
| 14 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent ASIC/certificates/authority evidence** |
| 15 | Tax/IP | settled under general regime | **Keep OPEN and separate** |

**Headline message to the Seller:** we do not accept the "[STANDARD]/FINAL/already agreed" framing — there is no principal-level agreement on our side, and your own Disclosure Letter (para 11) confirms no position is settled. The two most important structural fights are (a) restoring a **separate Fundamental/Title/Tax regime** (the "administrative simplicity" merger and the "applies to all Claims" sweeper are unacceptable) and (b) a **non-waivable fraud/deliberate-misconduct carve-out**. The two most important live commercial protections are the **Bluefen consent condition** (30% of revenue) and the **Riverlark payoff-at-completion**, with the **bonus funding** and **export incident** close behind.

**Authority flag for the deal team:** the cap (20%) and limitation period (18m) both sit at our fallback levels. I have *not* treated either as cleared. If we decide to concede to those, each needs Amelia Frost's written approval identifying this specific draft before we move. Want me to draft the mark-up or a response letter on these points?
